title: Present perfect continuous and present perfect
summary: Present perfect continuous (процесс и его следы, длительность, временность) против present perfect (результат, количество, завершённость), глаголы состояния и случаи, когда допустимы обе формы.
ru:
## Процесс или результат
Оба времени связывают прошлое с настоящим, но **смотрят на него по-разному**. **Present perfect continuous** (have been doing) фокусируется на **самом процессе**: он мог только что закончиться, а его следы заметны, либо он ещё идёт. **Present perfect simple** (have done) фокусируется на **результате или количестве**.
> I've been cleaning the garage. — Я убирался в гараже. (процесс; вся одежда в пыли)
> I've cleaned the garage. — Я убрал гараж. (результат; можно ставить машину)
> You look exhausted. Have you been working all night? — Ты выглядишь измотанным. Ты что, работал всю ночь?

## How long? и How many / how much?
**How long** (сколько времени) спрашивает о длительности и сочетается с continuous, **how many / how much** (сколько штук) — о количестве и требует simple.
> How long have you been learning Korean? — Как давно ты учишь корейский?
> How many chapters have you read? — Сколько глав ты прочитал?
Нельзя: ~~I've been reading five chapters.~~ → I've **read** five chapters. Если у действия есть **счётное количество**, обычно нужен simple.

## Временное и постоянное
С **live, work, teach, study** при for/since обе формы возможны и значат почти одно и то же. Но continuous подчёркивает **временность или недавнее начало**, а simple — постоянство.
> My uncle has lived in Tashkent all his life. — Мой дядя прожил в Ташкенте всю жизнь. (постоянно)
> My uncle has been living in Tashkent since the spring. — Мой дядя живёт в Ташкенте с весны. (пока, неизвестно, надолго ли)

## Повторяемость и незавершённость
Continuous хорошо передаёт **повторяющиеся действия** за период (**I've been going to the gym twice a week**) и намекает, что **работа не окончена** (**I've been writing my essay** — возможно, ещё не дописал). Simple, наоборот, подразумевает завершение: **I've written my essay**.
> She's been taking antibiotics for a week. — Она принимает антибиотики уже неделю (курс идёт).
И осторожно: **single event + result** — это simple: **I've broken my glasses** (~~I've been breaking my glasses~~).

## Глаголы состояния
Глаголы **know, be, have (owning), belong, own, like, want, need** обычно **не ставятся** в continuous, даже если есть for/since — используем simple.
> I've known her for years. — Я знаю её много лет.
> We've had this house since 2016. — Дом у нас с 2016 года.
- ~~I've been knowing him since school.~~ → I've **known** him since school.

## Когда годятся обе формы
С **recently, lately, all day, all morning, for ages** различие часто незаметно:
> I've been feeling / I've felt tired lately. — В последнее время я чувствую усталость.
В этих случаях continuous придаёт оттенок «в течение этого периода», simple — «в итоге».

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~How long are you living here?~~ → How long **have you been living** here?
- ~~I've been having this car for years.~~ → I've **had** this car for years.
- ~~How many books have you been reading?~~ → How many books **have you read**?
en:
## Process or result
Both tenses link the past with the present, but they **look at it differently**. **Present perfect continuous** (have been doing) focuses on **the activity itself**: it may have just stopped, with visible traces, or it may still be going on. **Present perfect simple** (have done) focuses on **the result or the amount**.
> I've been cleaning the garage. (the process; my clothes are dusty)
> I've cleaned the garage. (the result; you can park the car)
> You look exhausted. Have you been working all night?

## How long? and How many / how much?
**How long** asks about duration and goes with continuous; **how many / how much** asks about quantity and needs simple.
> How long have you been learning Korean?
> How many chapters have you read?
Not: ~~I've been reading five chapters.~~ → I've **read** five chapters. When the action has a **countable amount**, we normally need simple.

## Temporary and permanent
With **live, work, teach, study** and for/since, both forms are possible and mean almost the same. But continuous stresses **temporariness or a recent start**, while simple suggests permanence.
> My uncle has lived in Tashkent all his life. (permanent)
> My uncle has been living in Tashkent since the spring. (for now; we don't know how long)

## Repetition and incompleteness
Continuous is good for **repeated actions** over a period (**I've been going to the gym twice a week**) and hints that **the job is not finished** (**I've been writing my essay** - maybe I have not completed it). Simple, on the other hand, implies completion: **I've written my essay**.
> She's been taking antibiotics for a week. (the course is still going)
But beware: a **single event + result** needs simple: **I've broken my glasses** (~~I've been breaking my glasses~~).

## State verbs
**Know, be, have (owning), belong, own, like, want, need** are normally **not** used in the continuous, even with for/since - we use simple.
> I've known her for years.
> We've had this house since 2016.
- ~~I've been knowing him since school.~~ → I've **known** him since school.

## When both are fine
With **recently, lately, all day, all morning, for ages** the difference is often small:
> I've been feeling / I've felt tired lately.
Continuous adds 'during this period', simple adds 'the overall result'.

## Common mistakes
- ~~How long are you living here?~~ → How long **have you been living** here?
- ~~I've been having this car for years.~~ → I've **had** this car for years.
- ~~How many books have you been reading?~~ → How many books **have you read**?
structure:
## Формы
| | Утверждение | Отрицание | Вопрос |
|---|---|---|---|
| Present perfect simple | She has worked. | She hasn't worked. | Has she worked? |
| Present perfect continuous | She has been working. | She hasn't been working. | Has she been working? |

## Формулы
> have/has + **been + V-ing** → процесс, длительность, следы
> They've been arguing for an hour.

> have/has + **V3** → результат, количество, завершённость
> They've signed the contract.

## Сравнительная таблица
| Значение | Present perfect continuous | Present perfect simple |
|---|---|---|
| Акцент | процесс | результат |
| Вопрос | How long...? | How many / how much...? |
| Завершённость | возможно, не закончено | закончено |
| Повторяемость | Я постоянно хожу в зал | Я сходил в зал 3 раза |
| Состояние | не используется | I've known / had / been |
| Пример | I've been painting the fence. | I've painted the fence. |

## Типичные пары
| Continuous | Simple |
|---|---|
| He's been running. (запыхался) | He's run five kilometres. |
| It's been raining. (мокро) | It's rained twice this week. |
| I've been waiting for an hour. | I've waited long enough! |
| She's been living here since May. | She's lived here all her life. |

exercises.title: Continuous или simple?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте глагол в present perfect continuous или present perfect simple.
exercises.example: Why are your hands covered in paint? — I (paint) the kitchen. → I've been painting the kitchen.

items.text: Why are your hands covered in paint? - I {{have been painting|'ve been painting}} the kitchen.
I {{have painted|'ve painted}} the kitchen - come and see how it looks!
She {{has been writing|'s been writing}} her thesis for three years, and it still isn't finished.
He {{has written|'s written}} twelve chapters so far.
How many emails {{have you sent}} this morning?
The road is wet - it {{has been raining|'s been raining}}.
I {{have been waiting|'ve been waiting|have waited|'ve waited}} for over an hour, and nobody has answered my question.

exercises.title: Результат, процесс, состояние
exercises.instruction: Вставьте глагол в present perfect continuous или present perfect simple.

items.text: You're out of breath. {{Have you been running}}?
Prices {{have risen|'ve risen}} by 8% since January.
I {{have known|'ve known}} Dev since we were at school.
She {{has been teaching|'s been teaching|has taught|'s taught}} at this school since 2009.
Someone {{has been using|'s been using}} my laptop - the chair is still warm.
I {{have read|'ve read}} three chapters of this book today.
We {{have been looking|'ve been looking}} for a flat since March, but we {{haven't found|have not found}} anything.
How much money {{have you spent}} on this project?

exercises.title: Выберите правильную форму
exercises.instruction: Выберите вариант, который лучше всего подходит по смыслу.

items.why: Видны следы недавнего процесса — **has been crying**.
Know — глагол состояния, continuous не нужен: **have you known**.

items.q: The kids are filthy - they ___ in the garden.
items.why: Следы процесса в настоящем — **have been playing**.

items.q: I ___ this car for ten years; I'm thinking of selling it.
She ___ the report. You can send it to the client now.
I ___ to call her for days, but I keep forgetting.
items.why: Длительность и повторяющееся намерение — **have been meaning to**.

items.q: The company ___ three branches this year.

options: I've been knowing him for years.
I've been breaking my glasses, so I can't read.
I've broken my glasses, so I can't read.
How long have you been living here?
How long are you living here?
items.why: How long + период до сих пор — **present perfect (continuous)**.

options: I have been having this car since 2015.
I have had this car since 2015.
How many books have you been reading this year?
How many books have you read this year?
I've been waiting for you since two o'clock.
I'm waiting for you since two o'clock.
items.why: Since требует present perfect, а не present continuous.

exercises.title: Составьте предложения
exercises.instruction: Составьте предложение из слов в present perfect continuous или present perfect simple.

answers: How long have you been waiting here?
She has been working for the BBC since 2012.
She's been working for the BBC since 2012.
She has worked for the BBC since 2012.
She's worked for the BBC since 2012.

items.prompt: (I / read / this novel / all week / but / I / not / finish / it)
answers: I have been reading this novel all week, but I haven't finished it.
I've been reading this novel all week, but I haven't finished it.
I have been reading this novel all week, but I have not finished it.
I've been reading this novel all week, but I have not finished it.

items.prompt: (they / build / the bridge / for two years)
answers: They have been building the bridge for two years.
They've been building the bridge for two years.

items.prompt: (how many / paintings / the artist / sell / this year?)
answers: How many paintings has the artist sold this year?
My phone has been ringing all morning.
My phone's been ringing all morning.

items.prompt: (I / not / have / a day off / since January)
answers: I haven't had a day off since January.
I have not had a day off since January.

exercises.title: Перепишите предложение
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя present perfect (simple или continuous) и слова в скобках.

items.prompt: We moved to this city in 2014 and still live here. (live / since 2014)
answers: We have lived in this city since 2014.
We've lived in this city since 2014.
We have been living in this city since 2014.
We've been living in this city since 2014.

items.prompt: The last time I ate meat was a year ago. (eat / for a year)
answers: I haven't eaten meat for a year.
I have not eaten meat for a year.

items.prompt: I started learning the guitar in March and I'm still learning. (since March)
answers: I have been learning the guitar since March.
I've been learning the guitar since March.

items.prompt: The phone began ringing an hour ago and it hasn't stopped. (for an hour)
answers: The phone has been ringing for an hour.
The phone's been ringing for an hour.

items.prompt: It started raining at noon and it's still raining. (since noon)
answers: It has been raining since noon.
It's been raining since noon.

items.prompt: Ask about the number: She has written some emails today.
answers: How many emails has she written today?

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте на вопросы полными предложениями на английском, используя present perfect simple или continuous.

items.prompt: How long have you been learning English? What have you been doing to improve it?
items.sample: I've been learning English for about five years. I've been reading articles and watching films in English.

items.prompt: What have you achieved this week? Mention a number.
items.sample: I've finished two projects and I've written about fifteen emails.

items.prompt: Describe something you have been doing regularly lately.
items.sample: I've been going for a walk every evening after work.

items.prompt: How long have you lived in your current home? Do you plan to stay?
items.sample: I've lived here for six years, and I'd like to stay a few more.

items.prompt: What have you been meaning to do for a long time but haven't done yet?
items.sample: I've been meaning to sort out my old photos for months, but I haven't started.
